items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Bob Dorough called me up and Al Schachtman

ctx.x: Yes, I have worked with quite a few and I'm thankful that I have. I worked -- I'm going to tell you one gig with Bob Dorough (PHONETIC). He's a pianist, singer, the one that said (unintelligible) he said he did some things with Miles, which he did. Bob Dorough called me up and Al Schachtman, I believe it is -- he was the guitarist with Nina Simone when she first hit the scene. They had a bar mitzvah to play out in -- it wasn't, not Queens -- out in Long Island somewhere. Well, it was right around the corner from…
I'm the only brother there and so when Al and Bob

start playing all these Jewish tunes, there wasn't no -- how did I know how to play it, you know? It just comes naturally to me because when I come up, like I said, hustling us-men around Chicago, we had to play everything. We go in clubs and somebody ask us, you know, for tunes. We've heard them. Somebody would sing them to us. We'd learn it right there, you know? That stuck back in my memory bank, you might say. Just like Clifford Jordan and I had a job one St. Patrick's night, up in the 90s. They had Tootie…
